Mi núcleo está en la construcción de aplicaciones y arquitecturas escalables utilizando diferentes lenguajes y bases de datos. summary: Astro Health Monitor is an offline-first health monitoring web app for astronauts on long-duration missions. It gathers vital signs and health indicators (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, sleep, bone loss, radiation dose, immune markers), evaluates them against reference thresholds, and gives the astronaut a clear status (normal, caution, critical) with a concrete action to take. Because communication with Earth can be delayed or lost, all data is stored and analyzed on the device and synced to Mission Control when a link is available. It installs as a Progressive Web App on laptops, tablets and phones, the devices crews already use, and includes a flight surgeon panel to follow the whole crew.
details:
What it does: Astro Health Monitor tracks astronaut health indicators covering the five risks of the challenge: cardiovascular, bone and muscle, immune, behavioral/sleep and radiation. Each reading is classified in real time and, when out of range, the app shows a specific recommendation, so the astronaut can evaluate and act without waiting for Earth.

How it works: Readings come from a simulator (designed to be replaced by real wearables such as Astroskin, or by datasets). They are stored first on the device (IndexedDB), analyzed by a local rules engine and queued for sync. When a connection is available, they are sent to Mission Control (Supabase/PostgreSQL with row-level security).

Benefits: Works with no connection, which matters in deep-space missions where communication can be delayed or lost. One app runs on any crew device. It includes a daily check-in for mood, sleep and stress, and a flight surgeon panel.

Tools: React, Vite, Dexie (IndexedDB), Recharts, i18next (English/Spanish), vite-plugin-pwa, Supabase.

Considerations: offline operation, low cost (open-source stack), accessibility (large touch targets, status shown with text and not only color). All data in the demo is simulated and labeled as such. Bone loss and radiation limits come from NASA sources; the other clinical reference ranges are general demo values pending validation.

Use of AI: code and documentation were developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), under the team's direction.

Demo access (no registration): open the link once and wait a few seconds so the app is cached. Then turn off the network (airplane mode, or DevTools > Network > Offline), reload, pick a profile and enter its PIN.

Flight Surgeon 9999 · Astronaut One 1111 · Astronaut Two (ISS medical officer) 2222 · Astronaut Three 3333 · Astronaut Four 4444 · Astronaut Five (Mars medical officer) 5555.

All data is simulated.

Source code: https://github.com/Alexismpxh31/astro-health-monitor
dataRefs: NASA HRP – Hazards of Human Spaceflight
